turns.content: Stellar rotation axes are isotropically oriented in three dimensions. Inclination i runs from 0 degrees pole-on to 90 degrees edge-on, measured from the symmetry axis. Let N_low count stars from 0 to 45 degrees and N_high those from 45 to 90 degrees. We want their expected count ratio N_high/N_low.

Using the isotropic solid-angle measure and the inclination measured from the symmetry axis, derive the normalized density p(i) on this hemisphere and an expression for the probability in any inclination band.
Use that density and angle convention to calculate the proportional count N_low from 0 to 45 degrees. Give its exact and decimal values.
Using the same density and convention, calculate N_high from 45 to 90 degrees and form N_high/N_low. Give exact and decimal results.
Interpret the ratio as a comparison of expected star counts in the two bands. What does the angular geometry say about why the counts differ?
Check that the probabilities for the two bands account for the whole stated hemisphere. How does that normalization support your count-ratio calculation?
State the final N_high/N_low and explain how it follows from the orientation distribution and the angle convention.
